A.explanation: This is $50 \times 1.6 = 80$, the product of mass and vertical height with weight omitted, so it is missing $g$ and has incorrect units for work.

B.explanation: This is $50 \times 3.4 = 170$, using the 3.4 m plank length instead of the 1.6 m vertical height and omitting $g$, so it is not the gain in gravitational potential energy.

C.explanation: This is $mgh = 50 \times 9.81 \times 1.6 \approx 780 \text{ J}$, equal to the gain in gravitational potential energy on the frictionless plank.

walkthrough: Identify the useful data from the diagram: mass $m = 50 \text{ kg}$, final vertical height $h = 1.6 \text{ m}$, and plank length $3.4 \text{ m}$ along the slope.
State the rule: with no friction and minimum pushing at constant speed, work done by the push = gain in gravitational potential energy, $W = mgh$.
Explain why $h$ is used: only the vertical rise changes $mgh$, while the longer 3.4 m plank reduces the needed force but does not change the total energy gained.
Substitute values with units: $W = 50 \text{ kg} \times 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2} \times 1.6 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $50 \times 9.81 = 490.5 \text{ N}$ for the weight, then $490.5 \times 1.6 \approx 785 \text{ J}$, which rounds to about $780 \text{ J}$ with the given data.
